A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MultiFoley and provide readable text, equations, Figures 1–6, Tables 1–7, and Appendices A.1–A.3. No material gaps prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation benchmarks, control experiments, a 20-participant human study, and ablations, including the appendix guidance-scale results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original automated evaluations, human preference results, and main-text and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The DiT architecture, DAC-VAE, multimodal conditioning, masked training, quality tags, and classifier-free guidance procedures remain unchanged, including their Appendix A.1 descriptions.

E1.justification: Coverage remains VGGSound/VGGSound-Sync, Greatest-Hits, professional sound-effect/text training data, and Adobe SFX reference audio. Sound Ideas becomes HQ-SFX in the description, still with 400K samples; no changed domain or task coverage is documented.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Im2Wav, V2A-mapper, Diff-Foley, FoleyGen, VAB, Frieren, FoleyCrafter, and DAC-VAE. Table 2 retains the same FoleyCrafter variants and internal oracles, and Table 3 retains FoleyCrafter as the human-study comparator.

E3.justification: The 8,702-video filtered test set, eight-second generation, evaluation metrics, training budgets, and three-second conditioning/five-second extension protocol remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 retains the same human-study design.

E4.justification: The negative-prompting, conditioning-modality, quality-tag, fine-tuning, no-text, and guidance-scale analyses remain unchanged in Tables 2, 4, 5, and 7. The qualitative examples are also retained.

E5.justification: Both retain the same four-sample generation practices and human-study statistical reporting. Table 3 reports identical 95% confidence intervals, p-values below 10^-20, and N = 400 with 20 participants.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–5 and 7 and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, MultiFoley retains Table 1 CLAP of 34.4% and AV-Sync of 0.80 seconds, and Table 3 overall preference of 90.2%.

T1.justification: The conditional generative formulation, latent-diffusion loss, and guidance and extension equations (1)–(4) are mathematically unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified multimodal control, joint training on internet videos and professional sound effects, 48kHz generation, and improved quality and alignment.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic versus temporal conditioning, quality-distribution tradeoffs, and reference-based generation remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the limitations concerning training-data scale and timing multiple sound events.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 removes the Sound Ideas source name and URL, describing the corpus instead as proprietary licensed HQ-SFX data. This changes provenance and access information; the sample count, implementation settings, and Appendix A.1 training details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the missing Chung et al. T-Foley bibliography entry and connects the existing discussion to it, replacing the erroneous citation to Ament's Foley book. Other cited works and the substantive research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits replace Sound Ideas terminology with HQ-SFX, revise the dataset-description paragraph, and adjust wording in related work. The section order and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 updates its dataset label and caption to HQ-SFX. Tables 3 and 4 shift position within page 7, with accompanying text and bibliography reflow; the underlying displays and examples are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs the T-Foley citation and explicitly identifies the SFX corpus as proprietary/licensed. However, removing the Sound Ideas source name and URL makes the central 400K-sample training corpus less traceable. With scientific evidence otherwise unchanged, this produces a limited net loss in transparency.
